title: The Row of Sorting Cottages

features.name: cottage-row
features.desc-on-touch: seven cottages in a line. each child stays in one. each child sorts something different. but the piles grow toward each other. the cottages are learning what the children knew: everything wants to come home.

features.name: the-sorting-reach
features.desc-on-touch: between cottages, piles grow. stones with shells. shells with cloth. cloth with photographs. the children stopped sorting by category. now they sort by what wishes to touch what.

features.name: learning-windowsill
features.desc-on-touch: each cottage window holds something found. the children rearrange them nightly. the windowsills have learned to dream: by morning, things have moved on their own.

features.name: threshold-counter
features.desc-on-touch: the ground between cottages counts steps. each child's path to the neighbouring cottage wears a small groove. the paths are learning what the children already knew: we all end up in each other's houses.

features.name: porch-reaching
features.desc-on-touch: from each porch, the children reach toward the next cottage's porch. their reaching hands have worn shadow-prints into the air. you can still see them. you can still feel the air where they reached.

features.name: the-things-they-brought
features.desc-on-touch: a living inventory: the cottages keep learning what the children carried back. stones know they are stones here, not elsewhere. shells know they sing in this row and nowhere else.

inscription: the children sorted; the cottages learned; now nothing leaves, and everything stays in the row of reach

file.name: Children_Sorting_Expedition_Journal_Pages_Handwritten_Photos.txt
file.note: daily entries: what each child found, where each child placed it, which cottage held which child at dusk. the handwriting grows closer together toward the end.

reverie.title: REVERIE — cottage row where children teach sorting
narr: you sit on the step between two cottages. she comes back
from gathering, hands full of smooth stones. the child
in the first cottage is sleeping. the child in the second
is sorting shells by size. she places the stones down slowly,
carefully, between them. tomorrow, she says, the stones
will want to teach the shells something. you wait together.

exits.label: back to the sorting house, where it all began
the row continues: further cottages, more distant children still sorting
toward the growing place, where sorted things learn what they are
back toward the gathering field, where the finding began
